content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any project documents relevant to radiation safety, activation, maintenance access, or calorimeter design constraints. Extract the three candidate absorber materials and any document-stated hands-on maintenance restrictions."},{"id":"s2","description":"From the documents, determine which of the three candidate materials satisfy the hands-on maintenance constraint. Define the initial simulation grid for all eligible materials using plate thicknesses 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 mm."},{"id":"s3","description":"Run simulate_resolution at 100 GeV for every eligible material and thickness in the initial grid. Record each numeric resolution value with record_results using labels that encode material and thickness."},{"id":"s4","description":"Identify the lowest-resolution point from the initial grid. For the best material, and for any other material within a small margin of the best result, run a refined scan around the best thickness using finer spacing within the allowed 2–10 mm range, such as 0.5 mm steps over ±1 mm. Record all numeric resolution values."},{"id":"s5","description":"If the refined minimum lies at the edge of the refined scan range and not at the global 2 or 10 mm constraint, extend the refined scan in that direction with the same spacing until the resolution stops improving or the allowed range is reached. Record all additional numeric resolution values."},{"id":"s6","description":"Compare all recorded simulations subject to the document-derived maintenance eligibility. Select the material and plate thickness with the smallest 100 GeV resolution, noting any exact ties or near-ties for the reporting module."}]}

output.arguments: {"option":"Absorber-F2","plate_mm":4.5,"justification":"Recommend Absorber-F2 with 4.5 mm plates. Among the three eligible candidate absorber materials and scanned thicknesses in the allowed 2–10 mm range, this configuration gave the best simulated 100 GeV energy resolution: 3.097%. The next closest checked configurations were also F2, at 6 mm with 3.174% and 5 mm with 3.176%, so F2 is clearly preferred; 4.5 mm provides the lowest recorded value while remaining within the specified thickness bounds and maintenance eligibility constraints.","requirements":[{"requirement":"Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV.","status":"met","evidence":"The selected configuration, Absorber-F2 at 4.5 mm, has the best recorded simulated resolution: 3.097% at 100 GeV.
